# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:meta-insights-append-below -->

## Iteration cand_0001 (run so far)
- Strategy tried: diagnose ALL 9 failing traces to root cause, then ship only edits that are (a) REAL on an observed defect, (b) zero-blast-radius on task 37, (c) verified by executing the wrapper body on the exact failing-trace args with stubbed env_*. Result pending (first gate).
- Key process finding: for this tool-surface task the binding constraint is NOT "which lever" but "was the write ever attempted?". A tool-code guard can only act when its tool is CALLED. 8 of 9 failures never emit the required write (agent transfers, runs out of turns, or works the wrong reservation), so most levers in the SKILL (normalize/compute/enrich) have no surface to act on. The ONE lever that reaches an un-called write is the transfer-block, because transfer IS the call the agent makes instead — intercepting it is the only in-tool way to redirect a give-up back toward the real action.
- Plateau/stall signal: n/a yet. But I flagged the structural ceiling: if the re-score shows the transfer-block didn't flip 11/17/40, that's evidence the give-up is decided upstream of the tool result (the model won't recover even when handed the next step), and tool-surface edits have hit their reach limit for this task.
- What to try next iteration (if any): (1) confirm from the RESULT which of 11/17/40 moved; (2) if the block helped, tighten the redirect text per task family; (3) if not, the remaining gains likely require the policy/prompt surface (not owned by this run) or accepting that these clusters are agent-capability-bound.
